text: Multi-UAV Path Planning for Mobile Edge Computing with High-Density Mobile Devices
Lihan Liu, Hongrui Miao, Chunhui Qu, Zhuwei Wang, Haijun Zhang, Fellow, IEEE, Zhidu Li, Senior Member, IEEE,

Abstract—This paper addresses the challenges of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) assisted mobile edge computing (MEC) in high-density user mobility scenarios, a field that has not been extensively explored in current research. We introduce a novel deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework, named “ $j$ -PPO+EN-ConvNTM”, specifically designed to optimize MEC performance in urban environments with user mobility. The framework integrates spatiotemporal data modeling and spatial transformer network (STN) through an enhance Convolution Neural Turing Machine (EN-ConvNTM) module, which includes a three-dimensional external memory. It also features a joint continuous and discrete action decision-making module, termed joint proximal policy optimization $\mathrm { ( \it ) }$ -PPO). This design enables effective handling of the dynamic and complex nature of urban mobility patterns. The proposed approach extends the PPO technique to accommodate joint continuous and discrete action decisions, thereby enhancing UAV adaptability and efficiency in providing MEC services. Extensive simulations demonstrate significant improvements over all baseline models, particularly in terms of equilibrium efficiency and service continuity in highdensity scenarios. Our research addresses a critical gap in existing UAV-assisted MEC studies, which primarily focus on static or low-mobility user scenarios, and supports the development of more robust and efficient smart city applications, meeting the real-world demands of modern urban infrastructures.
Index Terms—High-density mobile devices, joint continuous and discrete actions, MEC, path planning, UAV.

This surge necessitates robust and efficient computing solutions, especially for applications requiring low latency and high bandwidth. UAVs offer a versatile solution to these challenges. Their mobility and flexibility enable them to deliver on-demand MEC services in various scenarios, especially where user density is high and dynamically changes [2]. UAVs can adaptively adjust their positions to maintain optimal service levels, addressing issues such as signal strength fluctuations and user demand variations [3]. Although UAVs provide a great potential, integrating UAVs into MEC architectures faces its own set of challenges. These include ensuring reliable and secure communication, efficient resource allocation, and effective integration with existing network infrastructure [5]. Moreover, the mobility of UAVs introduces additional complexities in terms of trajectory optimization and resource management, which are crucial for sustainable operation [6]. Addressing these challenges is essential to fully harness the potential of UAV-assisted MEC in high-density user environments, paving the way for a new era of smart city applications.

The integration of UAVs with MEC systems has been widely explored, but most existing research mainly focuses on scenarios with static or low-mobility users, inadequately addressing high-density environments. This limitation is critical because user mobility patterns significantly influence the performance of MEC systems. In high-density scenarios, such as urban centers or during large public events, user movements tend to be highly dynamic and unpredictable. This variability in user movement, in turn, results in significant fluctuations in computational resources demands and network connectivity requirements [7]. Current UAV-assisted MEC solutions can not be optimized for these conditions, typically leading to inefficient resource allocation, increased latency, and degraded overall system performance.

Moreover, the majority of current research fails to fully investigate the complexities of UAV trajectory control and resource allocation in high-density mobility environments. Efficient UAV trajectory planning is crucial for ensuring optimal coverage and service quality, especially when dealing with a large number of mobile users [8]. The objective is to develop an optimized framework that dynamically adapts to user densities and mobility patterns, ensuring efficient resource utilization and maintaining highquality service levels. This involves not only improving UAV trajectory planning and resource management, but also enhancing the integration of UAVs into existing MEC infrastructure to meet the unique demands of mobility user environments.

Our work presents a deep learning framework, termed “j-PPO+EN-ConvNTM”, designed to address the complexities of UAV-assisted MEC in high-density user mobility scenarios. This framework integrates spatiotemporal data analysis with advanced feature extraction via the “EN-ConvNTM” module, and incorporates a sophisticated decision-making process through the $j$ -PPO module, which handles both continuous and discrete actions. The EN-ConvNTM module features a threedimensional (3-D) external memory and a STN, enabling it to effectively capture and interpret long-term 3-D observational data [10]. This capability is crucial for accurate decisionmaking in dynamic environments, and is supported by a novel read-write mechanism specifically adapted to complex urban mobility patterns.

To the best of our knowledge, there is currently scant research on algorithmic solutions for multi-UAV path planning in the context of MEC with high-density mobile devices. This study seeks to fill this research gap, and the main contributions are summarized as follows.

II. RELATED WORKS

The integration of UAVs into MEC, particularly in highdensity user mobility scenarios, has become as a crucial research frontier. This integration aims to address the challenges of limited computing resources and the need for rapid data processing near end-users. Introduced to bring computational resources closer to data sources, MEC significantly reduces latency and network congestion [11]. In this context, UAVs have evolved beyond traditional surveillance roles to serve as mobile computing platforms [12].

The evolution of this field highlights a shift from traditional centralized cloud computing models to decentralized edge computing paradigms. Early works like Hu et al. [13] laid the foundation for MEC by proposing architectures for task offloading to edge servers. As demonstrated in studies such as Zeng et al. [14], the introduction of UAVs introduced a new dimension, enabling flexible, dynamic, and on-demand deployment. This transition is particularly crucial in highdensity scenarios where user mobility and service demands fluctuate significantly. Research by Qin et al. [15] and Mohsen et al. [16] further advanced UAV-assisted MEC, exploring optimal deployment and resource allocation strategies.

However, recent advancements in UAV-assisted MEC have predominantly focused on scenarios with low user mobility and density [17]. This leaves a significant gap in research for high-density mobility environments, which are increasingly common in urban areas and large-scale events [18]. Current studies often overlook the dynamic nature of user demands and mobility patterns, which are critical factors in optimizing UAVassisted MEC system performance [19]. In recent years, there has been a shift toward optimizing UAV-assisted MEC in highdensity environments. Studies by Wang et al. [20] and Liu et al. [21] have investigated the challenges of resource allocation and task offloading in such scenarios, emphasizing the need for intelligent algorithms to effectively manage dynamic and heterogeneous demands. Addressing these challenges paves the way for the development of more robust, efficient, and scalable UAV-assisted MEC systems that can meet the evolving needs of high-density mobility applications.
It is noteworthy that in high-density user mobility scenarios, the primary challenge lies in effectively managing computational resources while environmental dynamic adaptability.

B. POMDP Definition

To tackle the aforementioned optimization problem, it is necessary to develop a POMDP framework instead of a fully observable MDP. This is because the system's dynamics are inherently complex and uncertain. The POMDP approach is particularly suitable for environments where the state information is not fully observable, which is highly relevant to our problem involving interactions between UAVs and IoT devices. Factors such as precise UAV locations or internal states of IoT devices may be partially unknown or obscured.

Furthermore, the POMDP can accommodate the inherent uncertainty in action outcomes and observations, which is crucial in unpredictable scenarios such as UAV flight decision-making or IoT data transmission. Unlike MDPs that assume complete state information during decision-making, POMDPs use belief states, a probabilistic representation of the possible states of the environment, to guide decision-making under uncertainty. This approach effectively captures the real-world complexities of partial observability and decision-making under uncertainty, making POMDP a more fitting and realistic framework for optimizing operational strategies in dynamic and partially known environments involving UAV and IoT interactions.

The POMDP framework is characterized by a tuple $( \mathcal { S } , \mathcal { A } , r , \rho _ { 0 } , \rho , \mathcal { O } , P _ { r } , \gamma )$ , where $s$ represents the set of environment states, $\mathcal { A }$ is the set of actions, and $\gamma$ is the discount factor. The reward function is expressed as $r ( \mathbf { s } _ { n } )$ . The initial state of the environment is given by the distribution function $\rho _ { 0 } ( \mathbf { s } _ { 0 } )$ , with $\rho ( \mathbf { s } _ { n + 1 } | \mathbf { s } _ { n } , \mathbf { a } _ { n } )$ describing the state transition function. In this partially observable setting, the agent receives observations ${ \bf 0 } _ { n }$ from $\mathcal { O }$ rather than direct access to state ${ \bf s } _ { n }$ . The probability of observing $\mathbf { o } _ { n }$ given ${ \bf s } _ { n }$ is defined by $P _ { r } ( \mathbf { o } _ { n } | \mathbf { s } _ { n } )$ .

VI. CONCLUSION

In this study, we tackle the challenge of path planning for multiple UAVs in high-density mobile device environments with multiple charging stations available. The optimization problem is structured using a POMDP, and an innovative deep reinforcement learning framework named $j$ -PPO+EN-ConvNTM is proposed. This framework integrates $j$ -PPO, a modified version of the PPO algorithm supporting both continuous and discrete action controls. Additionally, it incorporates a novel sequential module, EN-ConvNTM, which leverages a STN to process and utilize extensive spatiotemporal sequences. Comprehensive experiments are conducted to evaluate UAV flight trajectory design, hyperparameter settings, and performance comparisons with four baseline models and existing DRL algorithms. The results strongly demonstrate the superior efficacy and performance improvements of our proposed solution. It is essential to recognize that the proposed $\scriptstyle j - \mathrm { P P O + E N } .$ $j$ - ConvNTM algorithm has undergone numerical simulations to demonstrate its effectiveness. Future work should involve testing the $j$ -PPO+EN-ConvNTM algorithm on a real-world UAVassisted MEC system to validate its practical performance, and other challenges, such as hardware limitations and uplink interferences, require further investigated.
